camera.position: the view is Nora's own eyes as she rides astride the juvenile Triceratops just behind its frill, facing forward in the direction it gallops; all recording gear is completely outside the visible frame

setting.location: Hell Creek floodplain forest, Montana, Late Cretaceous, 66 million years ago, warm humid late morning
elements: a humid riverside forest of broadleaf flowering trees and shrubs mixed with tall straight dawn redwood trunks; hazy sunlight slants in from the upper left; low ferns and leafy shrubs line a soft wet mud path with puddles; no grass anywhere; warm and humid, no snow, no frost

exactly one tyrannosaur is already visible at frame 0 at the left edge of the frame, about thirty meters ahead and to the left, striding out of the trees toward the path, its head and shoulders above the ferns; it stays the only predator in the clip, never appears suddenly and never vanishes
exactly two dinosaurs in the whole clip: the Triceratops Nora rides and the tyrannosaur; no other animals, no birds in the frame, no people

characters.name: Juvenile Triceratops

characters.name: Tyrannosaur
characters.visual_lock: matches the Tyrannosaurus reference image exactly: massive boxy skull, tiny two-fingered forearms, dark grey-brown pebbly hide with faint darker stripes and a paler belly, long tail held straight out level
characters.position: comes out of the trees on the left and then strides alongside them, parallel to the path, in the left third of the frame; more than twice as tall as the Triceratops: its hips are higher than the top of the Triceratops's frill; it moves at a heavy fast walk, never a run: one foot is always on the ground; its body dips and rises with each step, its huge thighs bunch and the thigh skin ripples on each impact, its tail swings slightly against each stride; its mouth is closed except during the roar

timeline_action.0-3s: From frame 0 the Triceratops is already galloping straight along the path and the tyrannosaur is already striding out of the trees at the left edge of the frame, about thirty meters ahead-left. By 3 seconds it has reached the left third of the frame, about twenty meters away, angling toward the path. Nora speaks from second 0, off-screen.
timeline_action.3-7s: The tyrannosaur draws level and strides parallel to them in the left third of the frame, closing to about twelve meters. From about 3.5 to 5 seconds it lifts its head and opens its jaws wide in one long roar while Nora goes silent and her hands tighten on the frill; its jaws close by 5 seconds. Then Nora shouts again.
timeline_action.7-10s: The tyrannosaur keeps pace in the left third of the frame about ten meters away and turns its head toward them slowly, over about one second, no sudden snap. The Triceratops keeps galloping straight. Nora finishes her line by about 9 seconds; the last half second is only the bouncing gallop.
